entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "M.V. Act") by the original Claimant in Claim Petition No.18/2008 against the judgment and order dated 15.10.2012 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Achalpur dismissing the Claim Petition.
2.
The Appellant filed the above referred Claim Petition with contention that, she along with her daughter was travelling in the Auto-Rickshaw No.MH 27 P 7280, from Achalpur to Paratwada.
The white Minidoor was coming form opposite direction.
The Drivers of both the vehicles were driving their respective vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
She suffered injury in the said accident and claimed compensation.
The Driver of the Auto-Rickshaw, the owners of the Auto-Rickshaw and the Insurance Company of the Auto-Rickshaw were impleaded as the Respondents.
The Claim Petition was contested by the Insurance Company by filing the written statement.
The Appellant examined herself.
No evidence was led by any of the Respondents.
By the impugned judgment and order the learned Tribunal rejected/dismissed the Claim Petition by holding that, the Appellant failed to prove the negligence on the part of the Auto Driver.

3. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, it was the case of composite negligence and the Claimant was entitled to claim compensation from either party i.e. from owner/Insurance Company of one vehicle or from owner/Insurance Company of both the vehicles.
The learned Tribunal considered the accident to be due to contributory negligence.
The issue framed by 3 fa26.2013.odt the learned Tribunal was not in consonance with the pleadings.

He submits that,
the impugned decision be quashed and set aside and the matter be remanded to the learned Tribunal for fresh consideration after hearing both the sides.

In support of his submissions, he relied on the decision in case of T.O. Anthony V/s Karvarnan and others, (2008) 3 SCC 748 wherein the aspect of contributory negligence and composite negligence is considered.
4.

entities.text: T.O. Anthony V/s Karvarnan and others, (2008) 3 SCC 748
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Insurance Company that, it was the case of the Appellant that, the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the Auto Driver and she failed to prove the same.
The Crime was registered against the Driver of unknown vehicle.
The learned Tribunal has rightly framed the issues and decided the Claim Petition and no interference was called for.
The Appeal be dismissed.

5. The endorsement on the Appeal Memo shows that, the Appeal is dismissed as against the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 pursuant to order dated 18.03.2014 passed by the Registrar (J.).
6.
In T.O. Anthony (supra) the following observations are made:-
"5. The Tribunal assumed that the extent of negligence of the appellant and the first respondent is 50:50 because it was a case of composite negligence.
The Tribunal, we find, fell into a common error committed by several tribunals, in proceeding on the assumption that composite negligence and contributory negligence are the same.

In an accident involving two or more vehicles, where a third party (other than the drivers and/or owners of the vehicles involved) claims damages for loss or injuries, it is said that compensation is payable in respect of the composite negligence of the drivers of those vehicles.

But in respect of such an accident, if the claim is by one of Gumphabai Sahebrao Shahane vs Mohd. Kalim S/O Abdul Gani And Othr on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162503286/
2 the drivers himself for personal injuries, or by the legal heirs of one of the 4 fa26.2013.odt drivers for loss on account of his death, or by the owner of one of the vehicles in respect of damages to his vehicle, then the issue that arises is not about the composite negligence of all the drivers, but about the contributory negligence of the driver concerned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. "Composite negligence" refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons.
Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrongdoers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrongdoers.
In such a case, each wrongdoer is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them.

In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrongdoer separately,
nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrongdoer separately.

On the other hand where a person suffers injury, partly due to the negligence on the part of another person or persons, and partly as a result of his own negligence, then the negligence on the part of the injured which contributed to the accident is referred to as his contributory negligence.

Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stand reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence."

7. The perusal of the pleadings in the Claim Petition shows that, it was the Appellant's case before the learned Tribunal that, the accident was the result of negligence by the Drivers of both the vehicles.
The issue framed by the learned Tribunal was in respect of rash and negligent driving by the Auto-Rickshaw Driver.
What is seen from the pleadings and the judgment passed by the learned Tribunal, is that, the Appellant was travelling in the Auto-Rickshaw.
This shows that, the submission made by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, the issue in respect of negligence was contrary to the pleadings has substance.
On hearing both the sides and in the light of the above observations, in my considered opinion, the matter needs to be remanded to the learned Tribunal for fresh consideration in accordance with law.
Hence, the following order:-
ORDER i) The impugned judgment and order is quashed and set aside.
ii) The matter is remanded to the learned Tribunal for fresh consideration and decision in accordance with law.
iii) The Appellant and the Insurance Company shall appear before the learned Tribunal on 20.04.2026.
